content.title: Route per-kind Turn behavior through turnBehavior
content.intent: This PR is a refactor. It moves every choice that depends on Conversation kind and on who opened a Turn into one table (`turnBehavior`), and adds a lint rule so new branches cannot spread again.

chapters.label: One table for Turn behavior
chapters.caption: Kind, Source, and the Automation flag now pick one behavior row that the prompt, tools, and delivery read.
chapters.body: Before, each site decided for itself: the prompt mode, `reportBlocked`, `noReply`, the review desk and others read `agentInvocationId` or `declaresResult`, and the Thread worker disabled subagents by hand. Now `executeAgentRun` asks `turnBehavior` once, from the Conversation kind, whether a person sent the input, and whether this is an Automation run [1]. The PR says behavior does not change. The review risk is whether kind plus Source picks the same row as the old `agentInvocationId` check for every Turn, and whether the new lint rule is sound.
asks: Why not derive this from agentInvocationId as before?

chapters.label: The behavior table
chapters.caption: Four fixed rows describe a root Turn, a person in a Thread, an agent in a child, and an Automation run.
chapters.body: `TurnBehavior` holds where the final response goes, the prompt mode, whether the Turn must end with its answer tool (`gated`), and which tools it gets [1]. `turnBehavior` checks the Automation flag first, then root, then non-person input on a child; a person's input on a task throws [2]. A person's input means a Slack or web Source (`isPersonInput`), which replaces two copies in `session-stop.ts` and `state.ts` [3]. `deliversFinalText` and `postsRunNotices` move here unchanged [4].

decisions.claim: A person's input on a task Conversation should fail the Turn.
decisions.concern: Before, such a Turn ran with root tools; if any web or Slack path can still write to a task, it now throws.

asks: Why is the Automation flag checked before kind?
Can a web user post into a task Conversation?

chapters.label: Prompt and tool gates read the table
chapters.caption: The prompt mode, the result gate, and each per-kind tool now read behavior instead of run fields.
chapters.body: The Automation result gate reads `behavior.gated` [1], and `assemblePrompt` takes `promptMode` instead of deriving it from `declaresResult` and `agentInvocationId` [2]. The tool context carries `turnTools` in place of `agentInvocationId` [3]. `reportBlocked`, `noReply`, and the review desk read it [4], as do subscriptions and user customization [5]. `finishAutomationRun` still keys on `context.automation`, which wiring sets only from the table [6]. The Automation row has `noReply: false`, which matches the old `else`.
asks: Is turnTools required everywhere a ToolRuntimeContext is built?

chapters.label: Agent tools bind after behavior
chapters.caption: spawnAgent and messageAgent are bound in tool wiring from tools.agents, not in the runner.
chapters.body: Before, `createAgentRunner` bound both tools before the Run knew its kind, using the `subagents` feature and `agentInvocationId` [1], and the Thread worker disabled `subagents` for a person's Turn [2]. Now the runner only passes the binders through the environment [3]. `bindAgentTools` binds nothing for `none`, binds `spawnAgent` unless subagents are disabled, and keeps `messageAgent` for `children_and_parent` even when the Turn is too deep [4]. The CLI binder switches on the same value [5]. The Thread integration test drops its `subagents` assertion [6].

decisions.claim: A unit test of bindAgentTools is enough to show that a person in a Thread gets no agent tools.
decisions.concern: The Thread integration test no longer checks this end to end, so a wrong kind or Source passed for a Thread run would go unnoticed.

asks: Does the production messageAgent binder use the new agents argument?

chapters.label: Non-person Turns on a Thread
chapters.caption: Kind plus Source treats every non-person Turn on a Thread as an agent invocation, which the old field did not.
chapters.body: The child-agent row now applies to any non-person Turn on a child [1], and the test pins a non-person Thread Turn to it [2]. The old rule keyed on `agentInvocationId`, which only the Agent invocation worker sets. By inference, an Event or timer Turn that the mailbox worker runs on a Thread had root tools with subagents disabled [3], and now gets the child-agent prompt, `reportBlocked` instead of the review desk, and `spawnAgent`. Event delivery to the Location stays root-only, since only the root row delivers there [4].

decisions.claim: Every non-person Turn on a Thread is an agent invocation.
decisions.concern: If an Event or timer Turn can run on a Thread, it changes prompt and tools, which contradicts the PR's no-behavior-change claim.

asks: Can a Thread receive Event or timer input today?

chapters.label: Lint rule for new kind branches
chapters.caption: A new source rule counts kind, Source, parent-edge, and declaresResult branches per file against a baseline.
chapters.body: `SOURCE_RULES` counts kind comparisons, person-Source checks, reads of `declaresResult`, and parent-edge fields used as conditions in `packages/junior/src`, and skips `kind-behavior.ts` [1]. `main` runs it with the shared baseline [2]. The baseline lists 54 legacy files with their counts, and a count can only go down [3].

decisions.claim: A per-file regex count is strict enough to keep kind branches inside kind-behavior.ts.
decisions.concern: A new branch passes when the same file drops another one, and a local helper such as isThread hides many reads behind one match.

asks: Does the rule flag false positives in code this PR did not touch?

chapters.label: How we know it works
chapters.caption: Unit tests pin each row and binding case, the rule has its own tests, and an eval checks a reply in an Automation thread.
chapters.body: The table test pins every kind and opener pair, the task throw, and the Automation row [1]. Binding tests cover `none`, both agent values, and a Turn too deep to spawn [2]. A task Turn still gets the review desk disabled with the `reportBlocked` hint [3]. The rule tests show which forms count and which do not [4]. The delivery eval sends a person's reply in an Automation run's thread and expects a delivered root reply with no `finishAutomationRun` [5].
asks: Is any test an end-to-end run of a Thread or task Turn?

chapters.label: What to watch after release
chapters.caption: Two new errors and child-agent tools on Thread Event Turns are the signals that the mapping is wrong.
chapters.body: A child Run with no Conversation row now throws instead of running as a root [1], and a person's input on a task throws [2]. Any Sentry event with either message means a path the table did not expect. Also look for `reportBlocked` or `spawnAgent` calls from an Event Turn on a Thread; any such call means the change in the previous chapter is real.

decisions.claim: A child Run without a Conversation row should fail rather than run as a root.
decisions.concern: If the row write can lag the child's first wake, the Turn now fails where it used to run.

also_changed.reason: Binder types move from durability to environment
Tests and fixtures pass root turnTools
